overview.implementation_summary: This focused follow-up reviews the publication subprocess I/O deadline fix at the exact current PR head. The deadline begins immediately after spawn and remains active across request delivery, direct-child polling, and output-reader completion.

evidence.explanation: Pinned Head code starts the deadline immediately after spawn, makes all pipes nonblocking, and starts the bounded request writer.
Pinned Head code checks timeout/cancellation while waiting for the child and request writer, and terminates the process group on an uncertain outcome.

key_changes.summary: The publication request is serialized and written by a nonblocking worker; the operation polls child status and worker completion under the same timeout and cancellation checks.

evidence.explanation: Pinned Head code keeps the operation deadline active during output draining and stops the process group/readers on timeout.
Pinned Head code bounds nonblocking reads and preserves overflow detection with a one-byte sentinel above the supported response limit.
Pinned Head regressions exercise a non-reading child with a request larger than the pipe buffer and a direct child exiting while a descendant inherits output pipes.

key_changes.summary: Output readers are nonblocking and bounded; timeout/cancellation is checked until both readers finish, after which response-size limits are enforced.
